# The third stop, also a defect of this run, and what it taught

**Named as a defect, as criterion 2 requires.** Three stops now, where a run that worked would have
had one. The first batch (record 4) asked what proves criterion 1 and took an answer the gate does not
allow. The second (record 22) amended the criterion to what this ticket can carry and still named
things that do not exist when the triage runs. Only the third found the actual shape of the problem,
and it was findable at the first: **a criterion cannot be evidenced before the thing it describes
happens.** Criterion 1 named a green `verify-delivery` and a review by `seen-reviewer`, and the review
triage is the gate that decides whether a reviewer is spawned at all. Reading the criterion against the
order of the stages would have shown that at record 4, before a line was written. That is the defect,
and it is one defect reported three times rather than three separate ones.

**Two returns is this ticket's own thrashing threshold**, which is why the run stopped here instead of
trying a third triage: criterion 3 names a second return on the same slice as the point where a replan
stops being a correction. The threshold held, on the ticket that wrote it, against the session that
wrote it.

**The answer, on Ruud's authority, 27 September 2026.** Criterion 1 is amended a second time, to what
a review can judge: the fixture walk, this journal's delegation, and the budget figures. What only
exists after the review moves to the follow-up ticket, with the real-ticket proof that moved there at
record 22. The reasoning is recorded rather than the convenience: the two clauses are not dropped
because they are inconvenient, they are moved because no evidence for them can exist at the stage that
was asking.

**What the two returns bought, which is the part worth keeping.** The first return was correct and
found a real hole: `question_open` was reading the clarify draft's list rather than a recorded decision
below its threshold, and nothing read CI at all, so two of criterion 3's five conditions could not be
reported unless a session remembered to declare them. Criterion 3 went from 0.48 to 0.66 once they
were detected. A triage that had waved the ticket through would have shipped a run that could not see
red CI. The second return cost an attempt and taught the wording lesson above. Both are in the record
as rework, and the first one earned it.
